raw_response:
I will plant the land in the wheat-maize rotation that I know best. In Quzhou County, that is the most steady way for me to use the whole year, keep grain in hand, and avoid taking risks on crops that need more market judgment or more delicate management. I will keep the same 10 mu in winter wheat first and then summer maize after harvest, because that fits the local climate, the water conditions, and the way I can manage the work myself. I will use improved or hybrid seed instead of saving my own seed, because I want more even emergence and more stable yield. I will plough before wheat so the straw and base fertilizer go in well, and for maize I will use rotary tillage after wheat harvest so I can sow quickly. I will put most of the fertilizer into wheat and maize as nitrogen, with enough phosphorus and potassium to keep the crop standing and filling grain. I will irrigate wheat more times than maize, because wheat in my area depends more on timely water at key stages. I will not spray often unless I need to, but I will still plan a few pesticide applications because aphids, rust, weeds, and corn borers can cut yield if I ignore them. My aim is not the highest possible yield; my aim is a stable harvest with work I know I can finish on time.
